note: Pegunigalsidase alfa (approved 2023) and three alpha-Gal A gene therapies (ST-920, FLT190, AVR-RD-01) all ran through the Gla-knockout Fabry mouse; only the enzyme has an efficacy comparison and approval.
label: Fabry disease (GLA replacement)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). FDA nonclinical reviewers (BLA 761161, 2023) judged the mouse Gb3 data nonspecific: TLC with primuline staining 'was nonspecific and nonquantitative', so the model side is weaker than the paper claims.
engagement.note: Repeat PRX-102 (pegunigalsidase alfa) dosing cut Gb3 in kidney, liver, heart, skin and spleen of Fabry mice; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: PRX-102 cleared tissue Gb3 in mice
engagement.quote: The repeat administration of the enzyme to Fabry mice caused significant reduction (p-value<0.05) of Gb3 in various tissues
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: first member drug in the Gla-KO mouse (the strain dates from 1997, but scoring starts with a member). Year is the 2014 online date.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tissue Gb3 reduction, mouse kidney (to 64% residual) vs patient renal PTC Gb3 inclusions (-84%)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. FDA nonclinical reviewers (BLA 761161, 2023) judged the mouse Gb3 data nonspecific: TLC with primuline staining 'was nonspecific and nonquantitative', so the model side is weaker than the paper claims. NCT01678898 results posted 2020-01-27.
engagement.note: In the phase 1/2 trial pegunigalsidase alfa cut renal peritubular capillary Gb3 inclusions 84% in classic Fabry patients, as tissue Gb3 clearance in mice predicted.
engagement.short: Renal Gb3 fell in patients, as in mice
engagement.quote: All 11 male and 1 of 7 female patients presented with classic FD phenotype, in whom renal peritubular capillary Gb3 inclusions were reduced by 84%.
engagement.reason: Renal Gb3 cleared as mice predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (comparison_stated false). Gb3 is the enzyme's own substrate, read as proximal. The mouse kidney cleared less (64% residual) than human PTC inclusions (-84%), so direction only. Gene-therapy members reproduced the pattern (ST-920, FLT190, AVR-RD-01: plasma alpha-Gal A and lyso-Gb3 in mice and in patients) without changing the status, so no extra entries.

engagement.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
engagement.note: NSF mice given human CD34+ cells carrying an alpha-Gal A lentivector raised plasma alpha-Gal A activity; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: While both experimental groups showed similar engraftment levels, only the therapeutic group displayed a significant increase in plasma α-gal A activity.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the NSF line's first use; vector was a sibling construct (LV-alpha-gal A/IRES/hCD25), so product_in_model false.

engagement.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT02800070 has no results posted (registry checked). Paired by us: Huang 2017 is the model side (LV/AGA-transduced patient CD34+ cells in NSF mice).
engagement.note: In FACTs (NCT02800070, LV/AGA, the vector later licensed as AVR-RD-01) all five men reached near-normal alpha-Gal A within a week, as the NSF xenograft predicted.
engagement.short: Patients made alpha-Gal A, as predicted
engagement.quote: All patients produced α-gal A to near normal levels within one week.
engagement.reason: Enzyme activity rose in all patients
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison; model and trial used the same LV/AGA construct, which is the voxeralgagene autotemcel lineage. Direction only, as mouse and human assays differ.

dose.magnitude_basis: NOAEL AUC multiple of the MRHD (1.9-4.2x) vs the dose used (1x MRHD)
dose.confidence_note: Model side and human AUC both from the FDA multidisciplinary review; tolerability at 1 mg/kg from BALANCE and F01/02.
dose.model: Six-month IV toxicology, mice and cynomolgus monkeys (pegunigalsidase alfa)
dose.note: Six-month mouse and monkey studies were clean (immune reactions aside) at 1.9x and 4.2x the 1 mg/kg human AUC; patients were dosed to 1 mg/kg without such toxicity.
dose.quote: No adverse effects were observed in mice or monkeys at doses up to 1.9x and 4.2x, respectively, the MRHD, based on AUC comparison.
dose.reason: Stated margin held at clinical dose
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the model stated a tolerability margin (NOAEL at 1.9x/4.2x MRHD by AUC) but no efficacy exposure target, so dose is scored on the margin half only. Patients got 1 mg/kg q2w (BALANCE, F01/02) with no non-immune dose-limiting toxicity. FDA excluded animal allergic reactions from the NOAEL as not predictive of human immunogenicity. Dated 2023, when the review made the margin public.

dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10284695): NHP GLP study at 3e13 vg/kg, 26-week study at 6e12 vg/kg; no human dose prediction stated.
dose.note: NHPs tolerated FLT190 at 3e13 vg/kg; MARVEL-1 stopped after two low cohorts (0.75 and 1.5e12 vg/kg) for business reasons, so no exposure target was tested.
dose.short: No human dose target ever tested
dose.quote: In NHPs, α-Gal A expression was consistent with the levels of hGLA mRNA in liver, and no FLT190-related toxicities or adverse events were observed.
dose.judgement: The NHP studies stated a tolerability margin but no human exposure or alpha-Gal A target. The liver-enzyme harm that broke the margin is counted once, in safety, because the NHPs did not predict it. Development was paused to favour FLT201 (registry why_stopped).

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA nonclinical reviewers (BLA 761161, 2023) judged the mouse Gb3 data nonspecific: TLC with primuline staining 'was nonspecific and nonquantitative', so the model side is weaker than the paper claims.
efficacy.note: Fabry mice predicted tissue Gb3 clearance on PRX-102; no patient trial yet.
efficacy.quote: The repeat administration of the enzyme to Fabry mice caused significant reduction (p-value<0.05) of Gb3 in various tissues
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the mouse efficacy track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: renal Gb3: mouse kidney residual 64% vs patient PTC inclusions -84%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA nonclinical reviewers (BLA 761161, 2023) judged the mouse Gb3 data nonspecific: TLC with primuline staining 'was nonspecific and nonquantitative', so the model side is weaker than the paper claims. FDA accepted renal Gb3 (F01/02) as primary evidence and BALANCE eGFR as confirmatory.
efficacy.note: Renal PTC Gb3 inclusions fell 84% on pegunigalsidase alfa; BALANCE later showed eGFR slope non-inferior to agalsidase beta.
efficacy.short: Renal Gb3 cleared; eGFR non-inferior later
efficacy.quote: All 11 male and 1 of 7 female patients presented with classic FD phenotype, in whom renal peritubular capillary Gb3 inclusions were reduced by 84%.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call on the endpoint: F01/02's registered primary was adverse events, so the efficacy endpoint FDA relied on (renal PTC Gb3, BLISS) governs as the PoC gate. The mouse predicted the surrogate, so outcome_tested comes from BALANCE (eGFR slope non-inferior to active agalsidase beta, -2.51 vs -2.16), scored positive though it is a non-inferiority result, not a placebo win. The mouse shows no renal decline, so it predicted nothing about eGFR itself.

patient_trials.quote: Based on rate of eGFR decline over 2 years, pegunigalsidase alfa was non-inferior to agalsidase beta.
reductions in plasma and urine globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) are seen.

To Assess Alpha Gal-A Activity in Plasma Over Time (ST-920; week 24 means 16-76 nmol/h/mL across cohorts)

efficacy.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
efficacy.note: NSF xenograft predicted Gb3 clearance in kidney and heart; no patient trial yet.
efficacy.short: Xenograft cleared kidney and heart Gb3
efficacy.quote: Importantly, only in the therapeutically-transduced cohort was a significant Gb(3) reduction found in the heart and kidney, key target organs for the amelioration of Fabry disease in humans.

efficacy.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record: outcome typed PRIMARY in results; mean change -3.555 (range -4.020 to -3.090), only 2 analysed; trial terminated when AVROBIO dropped Fabry. Model side Huang 2017 abstract.

patient_trials.quote: reductions in plasma and urine globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) are seen.

efficacy.note: FAB-201 (AVR-RD-01): kidney PTC Gb3 inclusions fell by 3.6 per capillary at week 48 (n=2, registered primary), matching the xenograft's kidney Gb3 clearance.
efficacy.short: Kidney Gb3 inclusions fell, as predicted
efficacy.quote: Healthy renal tissue would have no Gb3 inclusions. A reduction from baseline is desirable.
efficacy.reason: Kidney Gb3 fell in two patients
efficacy.judgement: The results record lists kidney PTC Gb3 change as a primary outcome alongside AEs, so endpoint_role primary; n=2 keeps confidence medium.

safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of non-immune organ toxicity
safety.confidence_note: Both sides read from the same FDA review; one immune-complex glomerulonephritis case is also immune-mediated.
safety.model: Six-month IV toxicology, mice and cynomolgus monkeys (pegunigalsidase alfa)
safety.note: Animals showed no organ toxicity beyond immune reactions; patients' harms were hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis, which FDA treats as outside what animals predict.
safety.short: No organ toxicity, as animals showed
safety.quote: The safety profile of PRX-102 is generally consistent with that of other enzyme replacement therapies. The main safety concern is the risks of severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, and infusion-associated reactions.
safety.reason: Silence held; immune harms out of scope
safety.judgement: Judgement call: animal allergic reactions to a human enzyme were excluded by FDA as 'not considered relevant to predicting potential immunogenicity in humans', so the species could not show the boxed-warning harm and its silence is no miss. The non-immune silence held.

safety.note: NHPs at up to 3e13 vg/kg showed no FLT190-related toxicity; no patient safety data public in a tier 1-3 source yet.
safety.quote: In NHPs, α-Gal A expression was consistent with the levels of hGLA mRNA in liver, and no FLT190-related toxicities or adverse events were observed.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; the first patient's liver-enzyme rise had been reported in sponsor and trade-press updates (tier 5) but no admissible record yet.

safety.magnitude_basis: NHP clean at 3e13 vg/kg vs transaminase rise at 0.75e12 and 1.5e12 vg/kg (20-40x lower)
safety.confidence_note: Registry results table, not prose: the quote is the verbatim serious-adverse-event term (1 participant in each of the 0.75e12 and 1.5e12 vg/kg arms; 'Myocarditis' in 1), not a sentence. Trade press (fabrydiseasenews) reports the first patient's liver enzymes were treated with methylprednisolone and tacrolimus.
safety.note: MARVEL-1 results: serious transaminase increase in both dose cohorts and one myocarditis, at doses 20-40-fold below the clean NHP dose.
safety.short: Patients' liver enzymes rose; NHPs silent
safety.judgement: NHPs can show AAV-related transaminase rises, so their silence is a miss: contra on the gene-therapy platform track. Paired by me; the registry posting (2026-08-06) is the first tier 1-3 record. Myocarditis counted with it.

safety.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
safety.note: GLP-style toxicology in NSF mice xenotransplanted with the LV/AGA cell product found minimal untoward effects; supported the Health Canada CTA.
safety.quote: Additional toxicology studies employing NSF mice xenotransplanted with the therapeutic cell product demonstrated minimal untoward effects.
safety.judgement: Opening safety entry at the first public statement of the tox study; FACTs had started in 2016 but reported no safety data until 2021.

safety.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Confirmed later by NCT03454893 results (2024-01-05): no SAEs considered related to AVR-RD-01, no aberrant clonal expansion, no RCL.
safety.note: No serious adverse events attributable to the LV/AGA cell product in five patients; conditioning-related events only, as xenograft toxicology predicted.
safety.quote: No serious adverse events (AEs) are attributable to the investigational product.
safety.judgement: Paired comparison; xenograft silence on insertional or product toxicity held over follow-up so far. Conditioning (melphalan/busulfan) harms are outside the model.
